tour.title: Step inside and look around, one room at a time.
tour.copy: Scroll to take the full tour: first Dimora Verde, then Dimora Blu.
tour.v1.text: You arrive through the covered veranda: a table, deckchairs and greenery all around. The perfect spot for breakfast outdoors.
tour.v2.text: A bright open space with a large corner sofa that turns into an extra bed when needed.
tour.v3.text: A fully equipped kitchen and a big table for the whole family: cook, eat and spend time together.
tour.v4.text: A double bed, plenty of wardrobe space and natural light: the quietest room in the house.
tour.v5.text: A single bed, an overhead wardrobe and a desk: handy for kids or for working on the road.
tour.v6.text: Two bathrooms with showers, one with a washing machine: no morning queues, even with a full house.
tour.b1.text: You come in from the small terrace with its wrought-iron table: an outdoor corner for coffee or an aperitif.
tour.b2.text: A sea-blue wall, the sofa bed and a French window that fills the room with light.
tour.b3.text: An equipped kitchen with oven and hob, Sicilian tiles and a wooden worktop.
tour.b4.text: A double bed, a mirrored wardrobe and fresh towels ready for your arrival.
tour.b5.text: A bathroom with a tiled shower, a wide washbasin and a washing machine.

faq.title: Answers that help you book with peace of mind.
faq.a1: La Dimora Verde is larger, 105 sqm and up to 7 guests, with a maximum of 5 adults. La Dimora Blu is more compact, 40 sqm and up to 4 guests, with a maximum of 2 adults.
faq.a2: Falcone Borsellino Airport is about 12 minutes away by car.
faq.a3: Yes, the nearest station is about 600 meters from the house.
faq.a4: Check the calendar in the Book section: dates with events are booked. To confirm, you can write to us through the form or WhatsApp.
faq.q5: Are the homes suitable for families with children?
faq.a5: Yes, the homes are designed for family stays. A crib is available on request, and we recommend sharing any specific needs before arrival.
faq.q6: Do I need a car during the stay?
faq.a6: A car is recommended for maximum freedom between the sea, airport and nearby places. The closest station is still reachable on foot.
faq.a7: Check-in is available from 3:00 PM. Before arrival you will receive the information needed to organize access, timing and practical details.
faq.a8: From September 16 to June 15, the homes can also be rented for temporary stays with a 9-month contract.

scopri.hero.title: Local guide: things to see, where to eat and nearby essentials
scopri.hero.desc: From La Dimora di Icaro you have the sea, Palermo, daily shopping and plenty of places to eat just a few minutes away. Here we collected our useful local tips in Italian and English.
scopri.neighborhood.title: Neighborhood and daily essentials
scopri.neighborhood.desc: For an easy stay: groceries, fresh bread, fish, pharmacy and shopping centres are all nearby, many only a few minutes away.
scopri.neighborhood.local.title: Local shopping
scopri.neighborhood.local.1: Fruit, vegetables and local specialties about 200 metres away.
scopri.neighborhood.local.2: Macelleria Di Maggio butcher, bakery, bar, tobacconist, gelateria and hardware store nearby.
scopri.neighborhood.local.3: Pescheria del Bivio about 750 metres away, with fresh fish.
scopri.neighborhood.markets.title: Supermarkets
scopri.neighborhood.health.title: Healthcare
scopri.neighborhood.health.2: Non-urgent medical service in Capaci and Carini.
scopri.neighborhood.health.3: Emergency rooms in Palermo: Cervello, Villa Sofia and Di Cristina.
scopri.neighborhood.extra.title: Extra conveniences
scopri.neighborhood.extra.1: McDonald's, clothing stores and pet supply stores nearby.
scopri.neighborhood.extra.2: Poseidon Shopping Center is the largest in the area, with Decò and over 70 shops.
scopri.food.title: Where to eat nearby
scopri.food.desc: A practical selection of bars, gelaterias, local shops, pizzerias and restaurants, from Sicilian breakfast to dinner by the sea.
scopri.food.breakfast.title: Breakfast and bars
scopri.food.breakfast.text: Bar Al Ritrovo, Duci Cafè Bar & Bistrot, Bar Prano, La Nuova Foresta and Al Baglio Gelateria are convenient options around Villagrazia, Carini and the seafront.
scopri.food.gelato.title: Gelaterias
scopri.food.gelato.text: Al Baglio Gelateria on the seafront, Gelateria Mannino in Carini and several gelaterias in Terrasini, especially around Piazza Duomo.
scopri.food.lunch.title: Quick lunch and local products
scopri.food.lunch.text: Da Carlo Piccola Bottega Siciliana, Oleificio Failla and U Zu' Caliddu are handy ideas for local products, takeaway or Sicilian lunch.
scopri.food.restaurants.title: Seaside restaurants
scopri.food.restaurants.text: Sferracavallo, Mondello, Terrasini and Castellammare del Golfo offer many options, especially seafood, often with sea views.
scopri.food.pizza.title: Favourite pizzerias
scopri.food.pizza.text: La Torre, Madre Terra, Le Terrazze, Vitale, I Cumpari, La Baronia, Vitina and Oblivion are among the favourites listed in the guide.
scopri.food.palermo.title: Palermo for lunch
scopri.food.palermo.text: For street food and local cuisine: Via Maqueda, Mercato del Capo, Ballarò, Mondello and Sferracavallo.
scopri.carini.title: The home village
scopri.carini.desc: Carini takes its name from the ancient Iccara, a city founded three thousand years ago. Walking through the centre you'll find a castle, churches and a history that few expect just ten minutes from the airport.
scopri.carini.card1.desc: A majestic 11th-century Norman fortress that towers over the city. World-famous for the true tragic story of the Baronessa di Carini, murdered in 1563. Don't miss the Gothic portal and the breathtaking views from the terraces.
scopri.carini.card2.desc: The heart of Carini's historic centre: a 15th-century church facing the main square, with frescoes and artworks of great value.
scopri.carini.card3.desc: The beaches closest to the house: pale sand, shallow waters ideal for young children and a small island you can swim to on calm days.
scopri.carini.card4.desc: Less crowded stretches of coastline a few minutes from the house: Torre Pozzillo, Torre Ulisse and the Costa Verde offer coves and unspoilt free beaches.
scopri.palermo.title: The Mediterranean capital
scopri.palermo.desc: Palermo is an open book of history: Arabs, Normans, Spanish and Greeks have left their mark everywhere. Best explored on foot, to the rhythm of the markets and gilded churches.
scopri.palermo.card1.desc: An extraordinary mix of architectural styles housing royal tombs and offering a panoramic rooftop view. A timeless icon.
scopri.palermo.card2.desc: One of the oldest royal palaces in Europe. Inside, the Cappella Palatina is a masterpiece of Byzantine, Arab and Norman art with breathtaking gold mosaics.
scopri.palermo.card3.desc: A baroque square in the heart of the city, the "Theatre of the Sun", with statues representing the seasons and the kings of Sicily. Perfect for a memorable photo.
scopri.palermo.card4.desc: The largest opera house in Italy. Even admiring it from the outside is worth the visit; inside, the acoustics are extraordinary.
scopri.palermo.card5.desc: Two Norman churches side by side in Piazza Bellini: La Martorana with its golden mosaics and San Cataldo with three red domes inspired by Arab architecture.
scopri.palermo.card6.desc: A unique and unsettling place: hundreds of mummified bodies preserved in underground crypts since 1599. One of Italy's most singular attractions, not recommended for young children.
scopri.palermo.card7.desc: The monumental fountain with mythological statues, and nearby the Ballarò and Vucciria markets: colours, aromas and authentic Sicilian street food, perfect for curious families.
scopri.palermo.card8.desc: Palermo's seaside beaches: Mondello with its belle époque lido is the most famous; Sferracavallo is more authentic, with a small harbour and excellent fresh fish.
scopri.beaches.title: The most beautiful beaches near home
scopri.beaches.desc: The coastline around Carini offers beaches for every taste: fine sand, rocky coves, turquoise waters and equipped lidos.
scopri.nature.title: Nature reserves and trails
scopri.nature.desc: Around Palermo you'll find forests, mountains and protected nature reserves: perfect for a day trip in the open air, with or without children.
scopri.nature.card1.desc: A wooded mountain that dominates Palermo, with hiking trails and the Sanctuary of Santa Rosalia, patron saint of the city. The drive up is panoramic.
scopri.nature.card2.desc: A vast woodland area, once a royal hunting reserve. Ideal for hiking, cycling and wildlife spotting. Also visit the striking Gole del Drago.
scopri.nature.card3.desc: The first nature reserve established in Sicily: 7 km of wild coastline, emerald coves and trails through prickly pear. No cars inside, only silence.
scopri.nature.card4.desc: A mountain reserve with caves, gorges and rich biodiversity near Piana degli Albanesi. Great for those who love off-the-beaten-track hiking.
scopri.nature.card5.desc: A hilly and wooded area rich in flora, fauna and ancient hermitages: an authentic Sicilian rural landscape, far from tourist routes.
scopri.nature.card6.desc: Fine white sand, turquoise and crystal-clear waters, spectacular cliffs. One of the most beautiful beaches in all of Sicily, ideal for families with children.
scopri.sicily.title: When you want to venture a little further
scopri.sicily.desc: Sicily is vast and every corner has something extraordinary. Here is a quick map of the main destinations for organising day trips or weekends.
scopri.sicily.ne1: Parco delle Madonie – villages and nature
scopri.sicily.ne3: Sanctuary of Tindari and Marinello Lagoons
scopri.sicily.south2: Scala dei Turchi – white cliff over the sea
scopri.sicily.south3: Piazza Armerina – Villa Romana del Casale
scopri.evenings.title: Easy ideas for the evening
scopri.evenings.desc: For a walk after the beach or dinner out, these are the most pleasant areas listed in the guide. For boat tours, choose the port based on the coastline you want to explore.
scopri.evenings.walks.title: Evening walks
scopri.evenings.walks.text: Peppino Impastato seafront in Terrasini, Castellammare del Golfo, Mondello, Molo Trapezoidale and Palermo harbour, Isola delle Femmine, Borgo Parrini and Palermo historic centre.
scopri.evenings.boats.title: Boat tours
scopri.evenings.boats.text: Terrasini and Castellammare ports for the coast towards San Vito Lo Capo; Isola delle Femmine or Mondello for Palermo's coast; Trapani for Egadi islands and hydrofoils.
scopri.cta.title: Ready to discover Sicily?
scopri.cta.desc: From La Dimora di Icaro everything is within reach. Check available dates and book your stay.
